chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Joining Mamie Smith's band in Chicago
summary: Back from Wisconsin, he joined Mamie Smith through a drummer, Clifford Jones nicknamed Guy Wattle.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well now, Happy, we're jumping ahead again.
Yeah.
We've got to get out of -- now, wait a minute. You were with Bernie Young's band in Wisconsin, and then you come back to Chicago. And now do you go out with --
Mannie Benny Smith.
-- Manny Smith. Now, how did you
happen to go with her?

Well, there's a drummer they had. When they came back to Chicago the second time, Hawk wasn't with them then. Hawk wasn't with them then. Then he said to me, said, well, there's a drum player named Guy [Wattle], which is the Creole name they called this fellow. We (unintelligible).
Would you spell that.
He was -- Clifford Jones was his real name.
Oh.
But they called him Guy [Wattle].
Well, how would that be spelled?
(Laughter and simultaneous remarks)
It's broken, you know. That was used a lot of that --
[End of Side 1] Side 2
So Clifford Jones, he knew you, did he?

Yeah, he was (unintelligible) looking fellow, but we saw these guys putting them sticks in their mouth and filling them up, he bought that to Chicago put them behind his ear, (unintelligible) helped them -- got that from --
Funny that's where Lionel Hampton
